svg.title: curl exit status versus HTTP status.
svg.desc: A hypothetical HTTP 404 response can accompany curl exit status zero: receiving the error page is a successful transfer. This is explicitly not predicted output from example.com. A separate bounded HTTPS command shows how to inspect actual headers and immediately print the curl exit status. HTTP errors can be made nonzero with --fail; transport failure may yield no HTTP response.
svg.text: curl EXIT STATUS VS HTTP STATUS.
Two numbers: transfer outcome from curl; response outcome from the server.
Hypothetical missing resource, without --fail (not the output predicted below):
Inspect an actual request instead; its statuses may differ from that illustration:
Read $? immediately. --fail makes many HTTP errors produce a nonzero exit.
No HTTP response? No HTTP status. Read curl's error message on stderr.
